data.narrative:
iQPS is a public-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Tetsuo Yasaka, Akira Sakurai, and Kunihiro Funakoshi. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 4 same-sector, same-stage public comparables: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. The median valuation across these four public Space & Aerospace peers is $5.2B, with a range spanning $840M to $40.0B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business models and scale within the sector. A public-comparable P/S approach cannot be applied because iQPS's revenue is not on file; while the broader Space & Aerospace sector trades at a median 25.3x price-to-sales across 6 public tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL), applying this multiple requires disclosed revenue.

The single-method triangulation produces a median estimate of $5.2B, with a conservative range of $4.4B to $6.0B reflecting reasonable band-widths around the median peer value. Key uncertainties include iQPS's actual revenue scale relative to peers, market share trajectory, and contract value realization post-IPO. The wide peer valuation range ($840M–$40B) underscores sector-wide variance; positioning within this distribution depends on operational execution and revenue visibility not captured in available data.
